question: The p-type material is formed by doping a pure germanium or silicon crystal with impurity atoms having _____ valence electrons. The element most frequently used for this purpose is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __three; gallium**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• P-type material__ is created by doping a pure crystal like silicon or germanium with impurities having three valence electrons.
 
• Commonly used elements for this purpose include gallium, indium, and boron.
 
• These impurities introduce holes as the majority charge carriers in the material.
 
• The doping process modifies the electrical properties of the semiconductor, making it suitable for various electronic applications.
 
• P-type materials are used in diodes, transistors, and integrated circuits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **N-type material:**
 
 
• N-type semiconductors are formed by doping pure crystals with impurities having five valence electrons, such as arsenic or phosphorus.
 
• Electrons are the majority charge carriers in N-type materials.
 
 
 
• **Semiconductor Applications:**
 
 
• Semiconductors are used in solar cells, LEDs, and computer chips.
 
• 
• They are essential in modern electronic devices for signal amplification and switching.
